affected: linux-firmware 20251125 / MES 0x83 era on Strix Halo
symptoms: GPU hang, gfxhub page fault, memory access fault, llama-bench segfault, blocked management processes
detection: Package version; dmesg page faults; firmware inventory and hashes
mitigation: Upgrade to distribution-fixed firmware (Fedora 20260110 line or newer validated package); do not treat a kernel update alone as sufficient
do_not: Do not make permanent firmware rollback the default modern recipe

symptoms: MES REMOVE_QUEUE hang and GPU hang
detection: dmesg contains MES failed to respond; workload stalls
mitigation: Move to a currently supported ROCm line; amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0 is only a legacy containment measure
do_not: Do not present amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0 as a current official requirement

symptoms: Compute instability, queue faults, incomplete memory behavior
detection: uname -r compared with AMD RDNA3.5 table
do_not: Do not substitute HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION for missing kernel fixes

affected: gfx1151 long-context prefill on reported ROCm 7.2.1 stack
symptoms: Up to approximately 41% lower prefill performance
detection: Matched llama-bench A/B build with GGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN OFF versus ON
mitigation: Keep GGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=OFF unless local benchmark proves benefit
do_not: Do not copy the upstream generic ROCm Dockerfile’s ON setting into a gfx1151 performance baseline without A/B testing

affected: Reported transition b8460 to b8933 on Mesa 26.0.2 and Linux 6.19.4
symptoms: pp512 decreased by about 39%; token generation stayed approximately stable
detection: Pin both builds and run matched llama-bench pp512/tg128
mitigation: Pin known-good commits and gate upgrades with benchmark thresholds
do_not: Do not assume a newer llama.cpp commit is monotonically faster

symptoms: Model fails during load or mapping
mitigation: Use --no-direct-io and/or --no-mmap; collect loader and kernel logs
do_not: Do not treat either flag as proof that the GPU stack is healthy

affected: Large GGUF buffers exceeding reported per-allocation behavior
symptoms: Model load fails although sufficient aggregate memory exists
detection: Force AMDVLK and compare with RADV using the same model
mitigation: Use Mesa RADV for large models
do_not: Do not infer aggregate free memory guarantees a single allocation succeeds

symptoms: Only approximately 15.5 GiB available despite much larger system RAM
detection: rocminfo pool size versus system RAM
mitigation: Use current fixed kernel/ROCm and official TTM sizing
do_not: Do not confuse this closed cap with intentional TTM/GTT limits

symptoms: rocm-smi or workload process blocked in D state
detection: ps state, sysrq task dump, dmesg, /sys/kernel/debug/dri
mitigation: Capture diagnostics before reboot; update kernel/firmware/ROCm as one tested profile
do_not: Do not repeatedly invoke blocked tools and overwrite useful timing context
